text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.2% today, continuing a downward drift from its peak earlier this week. The backdrop is mixed signals on crude prices: while Brent crude topped $109 following Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, U.S. oil has remained relatively soft at $101.91 per barrel, and traders are now betting on diplomatic progress in the Middle East that could ease supply concerns. For a refiner, lower crude costs can squeeze profit margins—the gap between what they buy oil for and what they sell refined products for—even if it sounds counterintuitive.

The refining sector as a whole faces headwinds. U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity, which is healthy but not exceptional, and the real pressure is coming from geopolitics tilting supply expectations downward: drone strikes on Russian diesel facilities are tightening global diesel supply and raising prices there, while the U.S. is simultaneously exploring alternatives like Indian refining capacity. This shift in the refining map—away from reliance on traditional suppliers—creates uncertainty for domestic refiners like Marathon about their competitive position.
